newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU extends probe into Vulkan subsidies.
newsitem.headline: EU extends probe into Vulkan subsidies.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it now estimated that German shipyard Bremer Vulkan had diverted 788 million marks in state aid, 200 million marks more than originally thought.

It said it believed four Vulkan subsidiaries had been the main recipients of the misused aid: mechanical engineering firm Doerreis Scharmann, shipping company DSR-Senator Lines, Dieselmotorenwerk Vulkan and Schichau and Lloyd Shipyyards in Bremerhaven.
The Commission had approved the aid for restructuring Bremer Vulkan's eastern shipyards, MTW-Schiffswerft and Volkswerft.
It said in a statement that it was examining whether to require the company to recover the aid.
The Commission opened an investigation in February into the suspected misuse by the Bremer Vulkan group of up to 588 million marks in aid.
"As already suspected at the start of the proceedings, a considerable proportion of the money went to operational subsidiaries, most of which were in economic difficulties," the statement said.
"The money should have been available for the restructuring and operation of the two eastern shipyards."
